column1: # Palestine, PA Dar al-Iftaa: the perpetual al-Aqsa Mosque table, printed on the perpetual winter
# (standard) clock all year -- UTC+02:00 fixed, never the summer clock -- hence `clock` differs from
# `zone` (Asia/Hebron, the engine's own civil zone, which does observe DST).
# Ruling R118 (owner, 2 Oct 2026): the authority's own printed town offsets apply to its al-Aqsa table.
# The whole table (366 days, every printed time) read from the two prints held, the 2012 printing and
# the 2026 yearly calendar's reprint, identical on every cell (archive/tables/manual/ps-iftaa/2026-10-02/,
# with the printed offset list, offsets.tsv); each town's table is the al-Aqsa table plus its printed
# offset on every time alike: Nablus + 0, Hebron + 1, Gaza + 3. Each is a unit (a table printed for one
# point, rulings R30, R44, R45), checked at the city's own point (the app's city).
# Split, forward in time: fit on the table on its printing year, 2012 (a leap year: every printed line,
# 29 February included), and on 2026 (the 2026 calendar's own print); held out, the table mapped onto
# 2027 (no 2027 calendar yet) and six dates of the Ramadan 1447 (2026) imsakiya, a third print. 2027
# held out was early by 1 min on a few days of Fajr, sunrise, Maghrib and Isha at al-Aqsa, Hebron and
# Gaza (a perpetual table against the leap cycle): those margins are widened to the three years' bound
# (Levant.kt). Class D (ruling R57): never early, at most 3 min late at al-Aqsa, 4 at the three towns
# on the events their own exception names.
